quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A shadow shrinking as a farmer's morning fieldwork stretches into midday"?
quests.hint: Think about when a shadow shrinks — as the sun climbs higher, or lower?
quests.explanation: Yes! Shadows shrink as the sun climbs higher through the daytime, toward midday.
quests.funFact: By midday, shadows are usually at their very shortest for the whole day!

quests.instruction: "A shadow long gone as a family's bedtime routine winds down toward sleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a shadow disappears completely, with no more sunlight.
quests.explanation: Yes! A shadow completely gone, alongside a bedtime routine, points to nighttime.
quests.funFact: Without sunlight, there's no way for a shadow to form at all!

quests.instruction: "A commuter checking a bright departures board before a busy flight, watch set to 'AM'" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the letters 'AM' — which part of the day do they belong to?
quests.explanation: Yes! 'AM' tells you this is happening in the morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Clocks have used 'AM' and 'PM' to mark the two halves of the day for centuries!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A traveler checking a quiet departures board before a red-eye flight, watch set to 'PM'"?
quests.hint: Think about the letters 'PM,' plus the phrase 'red-eye flight' — both point to the same time.
quests.explanation: Yes! 'PM' and a red-eye flight both point to nighttime.
quests.funFact: A 'red-eye flight' gets its name because passengers often arrive tired with red, sleepy eyes!

quests.instruction: "A nocturnal owl exhibit at the zoo, closed and dark, while afternoon visitors crowd the lion enclosure instead" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about which exhibit has the crowd — the closed one, or the busy one?
quests.explanation: Yes! The crowd at the lion enclosure tells you the zoo is open for daytime visitors right now.
quests.funFact: Some zoos flip their lighting for nocturnal exhibits so daytime visitors can see the animals awake!

quests.instruction: "A nocturnal owl exhibit at the zoo finally glowing to life as visitors gather round" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'nocturnal' — when are these animals actually most active?
quests.explanation: Yes! Nocturnal animals like owls become active at night.
quests.funFact: Some zoos flip their lighting for nocturnal exhibits so animals appear awake exactly when visitors expect!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A baker's fresh bread finally displayed in the window after hours of pre-dawn work". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what comes right after 'pre-dawn' — has the sun risen yet?
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the bread is finally displayed, the sun has risen and the day has begun.
quests.funFact: Some bakers start working many hours before sunrise so bread is ready first thing in the morning!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A baker kneading the very first batch of dough, hours before any customer arrives". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about what 'hours before any customer arrives' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Working hours before customers arrive means the day hasn't started yet — it's still nighttime.
quests.funFact: The smell of fresh bread can fill a whole neighborhood before the sun even rises!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A crossing guard's long shadow shrinking as the school bell rings for first period"?
quests.hint: Think about when the very first school bell of the day usually rings.
quests.explanation: Yes! The first school bell rings in the morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Shadows shrink through the morning as the sun climbs higher in the sky!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A security guard's flashlight beam sweeping a hallway long after the school bell has gone silent"?
quests.hint: Think about when a flashlight would actually be needed inside a school hallway.
quests.explanation: Yes! A flashlight is needed once it's dark, at night, long after school has ended.
quests.funFact: Security guards help keep school buildings safe overnight, long after students go home!

quests.instruction: "A weather vane spinning above a bustling farmers market, its shadow barely visible at noon" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about whether noon falls early or late in the daytime.
quests.explanation: Yes! Noon is the middle of the daytime, when shadows are shortest.
quests.funFact: At noon, the sun is at its highest point, making shadows barely visible!

quests.instruction: "A weather vane creaking above a locked farmers market, its shape barely visible under starlight" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when starlight would actually be the only light around.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sky dark enough for starlight tells you it's already night.
quests.funFact: A weather vane is often shaped like an arrow, a rooster, or another fun design!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A science class sketching a sundial's shrinking shadow as the lesson continues". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a sundial actually has a shadow to sketch at all.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sundial only casts a shadow using sunlight, so this class is happening during the day.
quests.funFact: A sundial's shadow moves slowly and steadily as the hours pass!

quests.instruction: "A tired overnight worker beginning her rounds just as the neighborhood settles into quiet" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a neighborhood would settle into being quiet.
quests.explanation: Yes! A quiet, settled neighborhood suggests it's already night.
quests.funFact: Night shifts help make sure important places stay safe and running smoothly, even while most people sleep!

quests.instruction: "A tired overnight worker heading home just as the morning rush begins outside" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the morning rush of commuters usually begins.
quests.explanation: Yes! The morning rush tells you the day has begun, even for a worker heading home to rest.
quests.funFact: Some workers sleep during the day and work through the night, on what's called a night shift!

quests.instruction: "A hiker switching on a headlamp, remembering trail maps are for daylight only" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a headlamp would actually be needed to see the trail.
quests.explanation: Yes! A headlamp is needed once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: A headlamp keeps a hiker's hands free while lighting up the trail ahead!

quests.instruction: "A hiker checking a trail map under bright sun, remembering headlamps are only for after dark" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what's making everything so bright and easy to see on the trail.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bright sun tells you it's daytime, so a headlamp isn't needed yet.
quests.funFact: Hikers often carry a headlamp just in case their trip runs later than planned!

quests.instruction: "A museum's nocturnal animal exhibit finally bright and busy, long after the afternoon crowds have gone" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what 'long after the daytime crowds have gone' tells you.
quests.explanation: Yes! Once the daytime crowds are gone, it's already evening or night.
quests.funFact: Nocturnal animals become their liveliest selves once the sun goes down!

quests.instruction: "A museum guide explaining nocturnal animal habits to a classroom full of morning visitors" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the classroom of visitors is actually there listening.
quests.explanation: Yes! The visiting classroom tells you the museum is open during the day, even though the lesson is about nighttime animals.
quests.funFact: Learning about nocturnal animals is a popular field trip topic at many museums and zoos!

quests.instruction: "The Earth's spin turning our side away from the sun once again" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what it means for the Earth to spin until we're facing away from the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! Facing away from the sun is exactly what nighttime means for a place on Earth.
quests.funFact: It's always daytime somewhere on Earth, even while it's nighttime where you are!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The Earth's spin bringing our side to face the sun once again"?
quests.hint: Think about what it means for the Earth to spin until we're facing sunlight again.
quests.explanation: Yes! Facing toward the sun is exactly what daytime means for a place on Earth.
quests.funFact: This constant spinning is why we experience a new sunrise and sunset every day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An owl's hoot announcing the sky's very first darkening"?
quests.hint: Think about what a darkening sky is turning into.
quests.explanation: Yes! A darkening sky signals the night is just beginning.
quests.funFact: Owls are famous for hooting once the sun goes down and the sky begins to darken!

quests.instruction: "A rooster's crow announcing the sky's very first brightening" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what a brightening sky is turning into.
quests.explanation: Yes! This crow greets the very first light of the day.
quests.funFact: A rooster's crow can carry for a very long distance across a quiet farm!

quests.instruction: "A phrase encouraging someone completely exhausted to finally stop and rest" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when someone would finally decide to stop working and rest.
quests.explanation: Yes! Stopping to rest for good usually happens once evening or night arrives. People often call this 'calling it a day'!
quests.funFact: Deciding to rest and try again tomorrow is a healthy habit!

quests.instruction: "A phrase encouraging someone to make the very most of the sunlight while it lasts" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what kind of light you would need for this phrase to make sense.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunlight is a daytime thing, which is exactly what this saying is about.
quests.funFact: Phrases like this have been passed down through many generations!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A porch light glowing to help guide the way up a dark walkway"?
quests.hint: Think about when a porch light would actually be needed to light the way.
quests.explanation: Yes! Porch lights are needed once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Some porch lights use a sensor that switches them on all by themselves as it gets dark!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A crossing guard's flag raised high to help children cross a busy street"?
quests.hint: Think about when a crossing guard would be out on duty helping kids cross.
quests.explanation: Yes! Crossing guards help children cross safely during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Crossing guards are trained to help keep every child safe on their way to school!

quests.instruction: "A stargazer explaining how a clear sky helps reveal the moon and every star" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the moon and stars are actually visible in the sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! The moon and stars are visible at night.
quests.funFact: A truly dark sky, far from city lights, reveals even more stars than you'd expect!

quests.instruction: "A tour guide explaining how sundials use sunlight to mark the passing hours" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what a sundial actually needs in order to cast its shadow.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sundials only work using sunlight, so this tour happens during the day.
quests.funFact: A sundial's shadow moves slowly across its face as the hours go by!

quests.instruction: "A bedroom finally quiet after the very last goodnight is said" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about what usually happens in a house right after the very last goodnight.
quests.explanation: Yes! Goodnight is said right at bedtime, at night.
quests.funFact: This simple tradition helps everyone feel loved before drifting off to sleep!
